description.narrative:
Sveriges Folkhälsomyndighet har i samverkan med Somalias federala hälsoministeriet inkommit med ansökan om stöd till Sida på totalt 40 miljoner kronor för perioden 2019-2022.
Syftet med ansökan är att inrätta en oberoende Folkhälsomyndighet i Somalia (National Institute of Health – NIH). Etableringen av NIH medför att Somalia för första gången kommer att få en självständig myndighet med ansvar för kvalitetssäkring av hälso-och sjukvården.
Det federala hälsoministeriet har fastställt den rättsliga grunden som är nödvändig för inrättandet av NIH. Denna process har godkänts av det federala parlamentet, statsråd och riksrevision tillhörande Somalias federala regering i februari 2019.
Folkhälsomyndighetens ansökan innehåller en detaljerad resultatramverk som är föremål för revision efter första året. Revisionen har till syfte att validera resultaramverket utifrån Myndighetens bedömning och egen erfarnhet av de operationella förutsättningarna i Somalia. Avtalet mellan Folkhälsomyndiheten och Sida reglerar bland annat Myndighetens ovannämnd åtagande.
Det övergripande målen för NIH är följande: - Tillhandahålla evidensbaserad rådgivning till det federala hälsoministeriet och till de regionala motsvarigheterna som ansvarar för hälsa och fungera som det nationella referenslaboratoriet för infektionssjukdomar - Förbättra katastrof och den allmänna beredskapen i landet avseende förutsägbara och icke-förutsägbara naturkatastrofer eller mänskliga katastrofer - Förbättra Somalias reproduktiva- och mödrahälsa - Utbilda framtida ledare som har ett evidensbaserat förhållningssätt till folkhälsointerventioner, hälsostjänster och hälsopolicy - Eliminera hälsorisker och förbättra mätbara hälsoeffekter genom ett hållbara civilsamhälles-och organisationspartnerskap - Fungera som nationell kontaktpunkt för internationella hälsovårdsregler - Genomföra andra mandat som tilldelas NIH av regeringen

The Public Health Agency of Sweden (PHAS) has in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health (MoH) of Somalia submitted a proposal to Sida with a total amount of 40 million SEK over the period of 2019-2022.
The objective of the proposed intervention is to establish an independent National Institute of Health (NIH) in Somalia. The establishment of NIH will mean that Somalia will for the first time in Somalias history have an independent authority with responsibility for quality assurance for healthcare.
The federal MoH has laid down the legal foundation necessary for the establishment of NIH. This process has been approved by the federal parliament, cabinet ministers and the auditor general of the federal government of Somalia in February 2019. In terms of more specific objectives for NIH, the following are stipulated in the proposal submitted to Sida: - Provide evidence-based advice to the Federal MoH and to the regional authorities responsible for health and act as the national reference laboratory for infectious diseases. - Improve the emergency and preparedness of the nation against foreseen and unforeseen natural or man man-made disasters. - Improve the reproductive and the maternal health of Somalia. - Train future leaders who have an evidence-based approach to public health interventions, health services and health policy. - Eliminate health disparities and improve measurable health outcomes through sustained community and organizational partnership. - Serve as the national focal point for international health regulations. - Implement other mandates that are allocated to NIH by the government.

The overall objective of the intervention will contribute to strengthening the Somali health system and its capacity to prevent and mitigate further deterioration of the health of the Somali population.
The specific objectives of the proposed intervention are:
- Strengthen the capacity of NIH Somalia to work with public health.
- Enhance the capacity of NIH Somalia with the purpose of strengthening the practice of public health, ensuring and improving the health of people in Somalia.

The Public Health Agency (FHM) of Sweden's collaboration with the NIH has focused on capacity building of so-called core functions of national public health institutes. The cooperation covered the following areas:
• organisational development including the preparation of strategic plans • monitoring of various health threats • management, analysis and visualisation of data as a basis for decision-making • investigation and research methodology • preparedness for various health threats, especially One Health
Within the framework of the collaboration, NIH and the Public Health Agency of Sweden have carried out joint activities in the above areas. The Public Health Agency has also worked closely with the Federal Ministry of Health and the State Ministries of Health, the NIH Board of Directors, the WHO in Somalia, IANPHI and the Africa CDC, as well as various public health agencies in Africa.
Statistics Sweden and SPIDER have had Sida-funded collaborations in Somalia during the same period. To achieve synergies, FHM together with Statistics Sweden and SPIDER has conducted workshops in statistics. During the project period, the partner has managed several risks, both security, corruption and political risks.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
